html:
The Occupation of Araucanía was the conquest of the independent Mapuche lands south of the Biobío River by the Chilean army, from 1861 to 1883.

For three centuries the Mapuche had kept their freedom in the Arauco War. The new Chilean state wanted their farmland and to join its north with its southern colonies. The army advanced in stages, building forts and towns such as Temuco, founded in 1881. The last great Mapuche rising was crushed in 1881.

The Mapuche were confined to small reserves, while the rest of the land was sold or given to Chilean and European settlers, many from Germany and Switzerland. Argentina carried out a similar campaign at the same time, the Conquest of the Desert. Mapuche claims to this land drive one of the sharpest conflicts in Chile today.
sum: The Occupation of Araucanía was the conquest of the independent Mapuche lands south of the Biobío River by the Chilean army, from 1861 to 1883.
